quizzes.title: CPI Measures and Their Significance
quizzes.passage: Inflation is an increase in the overall prices of goods and services in an economy over time. Indices are used to measure it, and the Consumer Price Index is one of the most important of them. The index measures the average change over time in the retail prices of goods and services consumed by households, so it follows the prices that ordinary families face in daily life. It also serves as a reference point for comparing prices across different periods. Economic indicators such as GDP and the Index of Industrial Production can be read against this benchmark to observe real changes over time. Every index is built on a base year, which is the reference point against which later prices are compared. Each item in the basket carries a weight that reflects its share of household spending. Over the years, however, the spending of households may drift away from the pattern recorded in that base. When this happens, an index that is not revised risks misrepresenting the actual price rise experienced by households. For this reason, the base of the index needs to be revised from time to time so that its coverage keeps pace with the present shape of consumer demand.

questions.q: Which range is the band around the current inflation target?
questions.explanation: The current inflation target is 4%, with a band of 2% (2% to 6%).

questions.q: In January 2026, which area recorded higher year-on-year inflation?
questions.explanation: Urban inflation was 2.77% against 2.73% for rural areas in January 2026.

questions.q: The Consumer Price Index is described as the main indicator of which kind of inflation?
questions.explanation: CPI is the main indicator of retail inflation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The CPI base year was revised to reflect updated consumption patterns and price structures.
Reason (R): Consumption patterns in India have shifted since 2012 toward urbanisation, services expansion and digitalisation of consumer spending.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet links the need for CPI base revision to the structural shifts in consumption since 2012.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a significance of the CPI base revision?
options: Lower number of items in the basket
Fixed base year for all time
questions.explanation: Base revision brings greater statistical credibility, along with better reflection of the cost of living and improved monetary policy transmission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CPI:
I. CPI reflects the cost of living experienced by consumers.
II. CPI is used by the Reserve Bank of India for monetary policy decisions.
III. CPI covers only goods and excludes services.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while CPI includes both goods and services, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CPI:
I. CPI is used for pension adjustment.
II. CPI is used for wage revision.
III. The current inflation target is 6%.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, but the current inflation target is 4%, so III is wrong.

quizzes.title: CPI Targets, Inflation Figures and Uses
quizzes.passage: Prices in an economy rarely stay still. Inflation describes an increase in the overall prices of goods and other items over time, and officials track it through indices. The Consumer Price Index is designed to measure inflation in the retail market, where households buy what they need. It records the average change over time in the retail prices of the items that households consume. Because it follows household purchases, it reflects the cost of living that consumers face. Every index begins with a base year, against which later prices are compared, and the items it covers are chosen to represent typical spending in that period. Spending habits move on, however. When incomes grow and lifestyles change, the purchases of households may shift to new products and new ways of buying. Without periodic revision, an index risks misrepresenting the price rise that households actually experience. Revising the base year allows an index to reflect updated consumption and price structures. Used over time, the index helps observers compare changes in the cost of living from one period to the next. Economic indicators such as GDP and the Index of Industrial Production are also compared with such indices to observe real changes over time.

questions.q: What is the current inflation target for CPI (in per cent)?
questions.explanation: The current inflation target is 4%, with a band of 2% to 6%.

questions.q: What is the lower limit of the inflation band around the target (in per cent)?
questions.explanation: The band runs from 2% to 6%.

questions.q: What was overall inflation (year-on-year) in January 2026, in per cent? (provisional figure)
questions.explanation: Overall inflation in January 2026 was 2.75% on a provisional basis.

questions.q: What was urban inflation in January 2026 (in per cent)?
questions.explanation: Urban inflation was 2.77%, against 2.73% for rural areas.

questions.q: Which central bank uses CPI for monetary policy decisions? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India uses CPI for monetary policy decisions.

questions.q: Which allowance is calculated using CPI? (one word)
questions.explanation: CPI is used for dearness allowance calculation.

questions.q: Which sector's expansion is cited among the structural shifts since 2012? (one word)
questions.explanation: Since 2012, India's economic structure has shifted toward urbanisation, services expansion and digitalisation.

quizzes.title: CPI and WPI Compared
quizzes.passage: Prices in India are tracked through more than one index, and each index serves a particular purpose. Inflation is an increase in the overall prices in an economy over time, and indices are the standard tool used to measure it. One index measures inflation in the retail market, where households buy items for their own consumption. A second index, the Wholesale Price Index, measures average changes in wholesale prices. The Consumer Price Index reflects the cost of living experienced by consumers. The two indices differ in several respects, so they should not be treated as interchangeable. Each index is linked to a base year, which serves as the reference point for all later comparisons. The coverage of each index is set by the items it includes, and the methods used to build them are not the same. Because the economy changes over time, the structure of each index has to be revised periodically. Economic indicators such as GDP can be compared with these indices over time to observe real changes. Careful reading of the figures helps users understand which measure suits a particular question, whether the focus is household budgets or broader movements in wholesale prices. Index numbers show how prices have moved relative to the base year.

questions.q: Which agency releases the Consumer Price Index?
questions.explanation: The CPI is released by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

questions.q: What is the base year of the Wholesale Price Index?
questions.explanation: The WPI base year is 2011-12.

questions.q: Which index does NOT reflect up-to-date expenditure patterns?
questions.explanation: The WPI does not reflect up-to-date expenditure patterns, whereas the CPI does.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Consumer Price Index includes both goods and services.
Reason (R): The Wholesale Price Index includes only goods.
options: Both A and R are true; R explains A
Both A and R are true; R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the WPI covering only goods does not explain the CPI's coverage.

questions.q: Which ministry's Office of Economic Adviser releases the Wholesale Price Index?
options: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The WPI is released by the Office of Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The CPI includes indirect taxes.
II. The WPI excludes indirect taxes.
III. The WPI covers services.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the WPI includes only goods and does not cover services, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The CPI reflects up-to-date expenditure patterns.
II. The WPI base year is 2011-12.
III. The CPI base year is 2011-12.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, but the CPI base year is 2024, so III is wrong.

quizzes.title: Agencies, Base Years and Coverage
quizzes.passage: Inflation refers to an increase in overall prices in an economy over time, and several indices are used to measure it. The Consumer Price Index measures inflation in the retail market, and it reflects the cost of living experienced by consumers. The Wholesale Price Index measures average changes in wholesale prices. Both indices are released by official bodies, and each one has a base year that serves as the reference point. Items in the consumer index include food, fuel and light, clothing and footwear, and housing. The indices differ in their coverage, so a reader should check the scope of each figure before comparing them. Price measurement must reflect changing consumption behaviour, since household spending changes as incomes rise. Without periodic revision, an inflation index risks misrepresenting the actual price rise experienced by households. Revising the base year allows an index to reflect updated consumption patterns and price structures. A revised index is therefore a better reflection of the prices households face. Revisions bring in newly added items and drop items that households no longer buy, which keeps the basket current. The index is therefore a running record of the prices households face, rather than a snapshot of one period. This is why the revised index matters.

questions.q: Which agency releases the Consumer Price Index? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The CPI is released by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

questions.q: What is the base year of the Wholesale Price Index? (format YYYY-YY)
questions.explanation: The WPI base year is 2011-12.

questions.q: Which ministry's Office of Economic Adviser releases the WPI? (name of ministry, short form acceptable)
questions.explanation: The WPI is released by the Office of Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.q: Which sector is not considered by the WPI? (one word)
questions.explanation: The WPI does not consider the services sector.

questions.q: Which kind of taxes does the WPI exclude? (one word)
questions.explanation: The WPI excludes indirect taxes, while the CPI includes them.

questions.q: Which office releases the WPI? (give the office name without the ministry)
questions.explanation: The WPI is released by the Office of Economic Adviser.

questions.q: Which ministry works through the National Statistical Office that releases the CPI? (abbreviation)
accept: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The CPI is released by the NSO under MoSPI.
